title: Electric Charges and Fields
syllabus: Electric charges: Conservation of charge, Coulomb's law: forces between two point charges, forces between multiple charges, superposition principle and continuous charge distribution; Electric field: Electric field due to a point charge, electric field lines, electric dipole, electric field due to a dipole, torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field; Electric flux, Gauss's law and its applications to find field due to infinitely long uniformly charged straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet and uniformly charged thin spherical shell

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Two identical conducting spheres carrying charges $+4q$ and $-2q$ are placed at a distance $r$ apart in air, experiencing an electrostatic force $F_1$. If they are brought in contact and then separated back to the same distance $r$, the new electrostatic force between them is $F_2$. The ratio $\frac{F_1}{F_2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Initial magnitude of force:
$$F_1 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{|(4q)(-2q)|}{r^2} = \frac{8q^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$$
When the identical conducting spheres touch, total charge divides equally:
$$q' = \frac{4q + (-2q)}{2} = +q$$
Force after separation:
$$F_2 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q^2}{r^2}$$
$$\frac{F_1}{F_2} = \frac{8}{1} = 8 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] An electric dipole of dipole moment $\vec{p}$ is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$. The torque acting on the dipole and its potential energy are respectively given by:
questions.solution:
For an electric dipole in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$, net electrostatic force is zero.
The torque acting about its centre is $\vec{\tau} = \vec{p} \times \vec{E}$.
The electrostatic potential energy with reference $U(90^\circ) = 0$ is $U = -\vec{p} \cdot \vec{E}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A point charge $q$ is placed at the centre of a cube of edge length $a$. The electric flux emerging through one face of the cube is:
questions.solution:
By Gauss's law, total electric flux enclosed by the entire cube is $\Phi_{\text{total}} = \frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}$.
By cubic symmetry, the charge is located symmetrically with respect to all 6 flat faces.
Flux passing through any single face is:
$$\Phi_{\text{face}} = \frac{\Phi_{\text{total}}}{6} = \frac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius $R$ carries a total charge $Q$. The electric field intensity at distance $r$ from the centre of the shell is:
options: Zero for $r < R$, and $\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$ for $r \ge R$
$\frac{Q r}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R^3}$ for $r < R$, and $\frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$ for $r \ge R$
questions.solution:
Applying Gauss's law:
1) Inside the shell ($r < R$), a concentric spherical Gaussian surface encloses zero charge, so $E = 0$.
2) Outside the shell ($r \ge R$), the Gaussian surface encloses all charge $Q$, yielding $E = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$ directed radially.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two infinitely large parallel conducting plates carrying surface charge densities $+\sigma$ and $-\sigma$ are separated by a small gap. The electric field in the space between the plates is:
questions.solution:
Each infinite sheet of charge produces an electric field of magnitude $\frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}$.
Between oppositely charged plates, the fields from both plates point in the same direction (away from positive and toward negative):
$$E_{\text{in}} = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0} + \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0} = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An electric dipole consisting of charges $\pm q$ separated by distance $2a$ has its centre at the origin along the z-axis. The ratio of the electric field at an axial point at distance $r$ ($r \gg a$) to the electric field at an equatorial point at the same distance $r$ is:
questions.solution:
For a short electric dipole ($r \gg a$):
Axial field: $E_{\text{axial}} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{2p}{r^3}$.
Equatorial field: $E_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{p}{r^3}$.
$$\frac{E_{\text{axial}}}{E_{\text{equatorial}}} = \frac{2}{1} = 2 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A circular ring of radius $R$ carries a uniformly distributed positive charge $Q$. The distance from the centre along the ring's axis where the electric field is maximum is:
questions.solution:
Electric field along the axis of a uniformly charged ring is:
$$E(x) = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \frac{Q x}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$$
Setting $\frac{dE}{dx} = 0$:
$$\frac{d}{dx} \left[ x(R^2 + x^2)^{-3/2} \right] = (R^2 + x^2)^{-3/2} - 3x^2(R^2 + x^2)^{-5/2} = 0$$
$$(R^2 + x^2) - 3x^2 = 0 \implies 2x^2 = R^2 \implies x = \frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A small oil drop carrying charge $q$ is suspended in stationary equilibrium between two horizontal parallel plates separated by $d = 2\text{ cm}$ when a potential difference of $2000\text{ V}$ is applied across them. If mass of the drop is $9.8 \times 10^{-15}\text{ kg}$ and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the charge $q$ is:
questions.solution:
Electric field between the plates: $E = \frac{V}{d} = \frac{2000}{0.02} = 10^5\text{ V/m}$.
For stationary equilibrium, upward electrostatic force balances gravity:
$$q E = m g$$
$$q = \frac{mg}{E} = \frac{(9.8 \times 10^{-15})(9.8)}{10^5} = \frac{96.04 \times 10^{-15}}{10^5} = 9.604 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C} \approx 9.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A charged particle of mass $m$ and charge $q$ enters a region of uniform electric field $\vec{E} = E\hat{j}$ with an initial velocity $\vec{v} = v_0\hat{i}$. The trajectory of the particle is:
questions.solution:
Along the x-direction, velocity is constant: $x = v_0 t \implies t = \frac{x}{v_0}$.
Along the y-direction, constant acceleration acts: $a_y = \frac{qE}{m}$.
$$y = \frac{1}{2}a_y t^2 = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{qE}{m}\right)\left(\frac{x}{v_0}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{qE}{2mv_0^2}\right) x^2$$
Because $y \propto x^2$, the trajectory is a parabola.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A hemisphere of radius $R$ is placed in a uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ directed parallel to its circular base. The total electric flux passing through the curved hemispherical surface is:
questions.solution:
The closed hemispherical volume encloses zero net charge.
By Gauss's law, total flux through the closed surface (circular flat base + curved surface) is zero:
$$\Phi_{\text{total}} = \Phi_{\text{base}} + \Phi_{\text{curved}} = 0$$
Because $\vec{E}$ is parallel to the flat base, $\vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A}_{\text{base}} = 0$, meaning $\Phi_{\text{base}} = 0$.
Therefore, $\Phi_{\text{curved}} = 0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An infinitely long straight wire produces an electric field of magnitude $9 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}$ at a radial distance of $2\text{ cm}$. The linear charge density $\lambda$ on the wire is:
questions.solution:
Electric field due to an infinite line charge:
$$E = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r} = \frac{2k\lambda}{r}$$
Given $E = 9 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}$, $r = 0.02\text{ m}$, and $k = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2$:
$$9 \times 10^4 = \frac{2(9 \times 10^9)\lambda}{0.02} \implies 9 \times 10^4 = 9 \times 10^{11} \lambda$$
$$\lambda = \frac{9 \times 10^4}{9 \times 10^{11}} = 10^{-7}\text{ C/m} = 0.1\,\mu\text{C/m}$$

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding electrostatic field lines is incorrect?
options: Electrostatic field lines can form closed loops
Field lines start from positive charges and end on negative charges
Tangent to a field line gives the direction of the electric field at that point
Two field lines can never cross each other
questions.solution: Because electrostatic fields are conservative ($\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} = 0$), electrostatic field lines cannot form continuous closed loops without violating energy conservation.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Three point charges $+q, -2q,$ and $+q$ are placed along the x-axis at $x = -a, x = 0,$ and $x = +a$ respectively. This system of charges is equivalent to:
options: An electric quadrupole with zero net charge and zero dipole moment
An electric dipole of dipole moment $2qa$
An electric dipole of dipole moment $qa$
A single point charge of magnitude $-2q$
questions.solution:
Total charge: $q_{\text{net}} = (+q) + (-2q) + (+q) = 0$.
Dipole moment about origin:
$$\vec{p} = \sum q_i \vec{r}_i = (+q)(-a\hat{i}) + (-2q)(0) + (+q)(+a\hat{i}) = (-qa + qa)\hat{i} = 0$$
Since both net charge and net dipole moment are zero, this configuration forms an electric quadrupole.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A uniform electric field is given by $\vec{E} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ N/C}$. The electric flux through a flat rectangular surface of area $0.2\text{ m}^2$ parallel to the $yz$-plane is:
questions.solution:
A surface parallel to the $yz$-plane has its normal area vector aligned with the x-axis: $\vec{A} = 0.2\hat{i}\text{ m}^2$.
Electric flux:
$$\Phi = \vec{E} \cdot \vec{A} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \cdot (0.2\hat{i}) = 3 \times 0.2 = 0.6\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A point charge $+Q$ is positioned at a distance $d$ above the centre of a flat circular disc of radius $R$. The electric flux through the disc is:
questions.solution:
The semi-vertical angle subtended by the disc rim at the point charge satisfies $\cos\alpha = \frac{d}{\sqrt{R^2 + d^2}}$.
Solid angle subtended is $\Omega = 2\pi(1 - \cos\alpha)$.
Electric flux through the disc is:
$$\Phi = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \Omega = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} [2\pi(1 - \cos\alpha)] = \frac{Q}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{d}{\sqrt{R^2 + d^2}}\right)$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An electron and a proton are released from rest in a uniform electric field. The ratio of the acceleration of the electron to that of the proton is equal to:
questions.solution:
Both particles carry charge of identical magnitude $|q| = e$.
Electrostatic force on each particle: $F = e E$.
Accelerations are $a_e = \frac{eE}{m_e}$ and $a_p = \frac{eE}{m_p}$.
$$\frac{a_e}{a_p} = \frac{m_p}{m_e}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Two small charged spheres carrying charges $+q$ and $+4q$ are fixed at a distance $L$ apart. A third charge $Q$ is placed along the line joining them such that the entire system is in equilibrium. The position and magnitude of $Q$ are:
questions.solution:
For $Q$ to be in equilibrium at distance $x$ from $+q$:
$$\frac{kqQ}{x^2} = \frac{k(4q)Q}{(L - x)^2} \implies \frac{1}{x} = \frac{2}{L - x} \implies L - x = 2x \implies x = \frac{L}{3}$$
For $+q$ to be in equilibrium under forces from $+4q$ and $Q$:
$$\frac{k q(4q)}{L^2} + \frac{k q Q}{(L/3)^2} = 0$$
$$\frac{4q}{L^2} + \frac{9Q}{L^2} = 0 \implies 9Q = -4q \implies Q = -\frac{4}{9}q$$

questions.question: A point charge $q$ is placed at a corner of a cube of side length $a$. The total electric flux emerging through the three faces of the cube that meet at that corner is:
questions.solution:
The electric field lines emanating radially outward from a point charge placed at a corner lie entirely parallel to the surfaces of the three faces meeting at that corner.
Because $\vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = 0$ on each of these three adjacent faces, the electric flux through them is zero.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] An electric dipole of dipole moment $p$ is aligned at an angle of $60^\circ$ with a uniform electric field $E$. The work done in rotating the dipole from this orientation to an orientation aligned with the field ($\theta = 0^\circ$) is:
questions.solution:
Potential energy of dipole: $U(\theta) = -pE\cos\theta$.
Work done by external agent without change in kinetic energy:
$$W_{\text{ext}} = U(0^\circ) - U(60^\circ) = -pE\cos 0^\circ - (-pE\cos 60^\circ) = -pE + \frac{1}{2}pE = -\frac{1}{2}pE$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A solid non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ has a uniform volume charge density $\rho$. The ratio of the electric field magnitude at distance $r = R/2$ to that at distance $r = 2R$ from the centre is:
questions.solution:
Inside a uniformly charged solid dielectric sphere ($r \le R$):
$$E_{\text{in}}(r) = \frac{\rho r}{3\varepsilon_0} \implies E_{\text{in}}(R/2) = \frac{\rho R}{6\varepsilon_0}$$
Outside the sphere ($r \ge R$):
$$E_{\text{out}}(r) = \frac{\rho R^3}{3\varepsilon_0 r^2} \implies E_{\text{out}}(2R) = \frac{\rho R^3}{3\varepsilon_0 (4R^2)} = \frac{\rho R}{12\varepsilon_0}$$
$$\frac{E_{\text{in}}(R/2)}{E_{\text{out}}(2R)} = \frac{\frac{\rho R}{6\varepsilon_0}}{\frac{\rho R}{12\varepsilon_0}} = 2 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An electric dipole consisting of charges $\pm 2\,\mu\text{C}$ separated by $2\text{ cm}$ is placed in a uniform electric field of $1.0 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the field lines. Find the torque (in $10^{-3}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$) acting on the dipole.
questions.solution:
Dipole moment:
$$p = q(2a) = (2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C})(0.02\text{ m}) = 4.0 \times 10^{-8}\text{ C}\cdot\text{m}$$
Torque magnitude:
$$\tau = p E \sin\theta = (4.0 \times 10^{-8})(1.0 \times 10^5) \sin 30^\circ = 4.0 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.5 = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Value in units of $10^{-3}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$ is $2.0$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two point charges $+8\,\mu\text{C}$ and $+2\,\mu\text{C}$ are placed $60\text{ cm}$ apart in air. The distance (in cm) from the $+8\,\mu\text{C}$ charge along the joining line where the resultant electric field is zero is:
questions.solution:
Let the neutral point be at distance $x$ from $+8\,\mu\text{C}$:
$$\frac{k(8\,\mu\text{C})}{x^2} = \frac{k(2\,\mu\text{C})}{(60 - x)^2}$$
$$\frac{4}{x^2} = \frac{1}{(60 - x)^2} \implies \frac{2}{x} = \frac{1}{60 - x}$$
$$2(60 - x) = x \implies 120 - 2x = x \implies 3x = 120 \implies x = 40.0\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A closed Gaussian cubical surface of edge $1\text{ m}$ is placed in an electric field given by $\vec{E} = (100x)\hat{i}\text{ N/C}$, with its edges parallel to the coordinate axes and occupying $0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1, 0 \le z \le 1$. Find the net charge (in $10^{-10}\text{ C}$) enclosed within the cube (take $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}^2/(\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2)$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
At face $x = 0$: $E_x = 0$, so $\Phi_1 = 0$.
At face $x = 1$: $E_x = 100(1) = 100\text{ N/C}$. Area $A = 1\text{ m}^2$ with normal $+\hat{i}$, so $\Phi_2 = 100 \times 1 = 100\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}$.
For all other faces, $\vec{E} \cdot d\vec{A} = 0$.
Total net flux $\Phi = 100\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}$.
Enclosed charge:
$$q_{\text{enc}} = \varepsilon_0 \Phi = (8.85 \times 10^{-12})(100) = 8.85 \times 10^{-10}\text{ C}$$
Value in units of $10^{-10}\text{ C}$ is $8.85$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An electron of mass $9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$ is accelerated from rest through a distance of $2.0\text{ cm}$ in a uniform electric field of $1.82 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}$. Find the time taken (in nanoseconds) by the electron to traverse this distance (take $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the electron:
$$a = \frac{eE}{m} = \frac{(1.6 \times 10^{-19})(1.82 \times 10^4)}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} = \frac{2.912 \times 10^{-15}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} = 3.2 \times 10^{15}\text{ m/s}^2$$
Using $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $s = 0.02\text{ m}$:
$$0.02 = \frac{1}{2}(3.2 \times 10^{15}) t^2 = 1.6 \times 10^{15} t^2$$
$$t^2 = \frac{0.02}{1.6 \times 10^{15}} = \frac{2 \times 10^{-2}}{1.6 \times 10^{15}} = 1.25 \times 10^{-17} = 12.5 \times 10^{-18}\text{ s}^2$$
$$t = \sqrt{12.5} \times 10^{-9}\text{ s} \approx 3.535 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s} = 3.54\text{ ns}$$
*(Recalculating value: $\sqrt{12.5} \approx 3.54\text{ ns}$, setting correctValue to 3.54)*

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two identical small metal spheres carrying identical charges are suspended by non-conducting strings of equal length $l = 1\text{ m}$ from a common point. When in equilibrium, the angle between the two strings is $90^\circ$. If each sphere has mass $m = 10\text{ g}$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find the magnitude of charge (in $\mu\text{C}$) on each sphere (rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
When angle between strings is $90^\circ$, each string makes $\theta = 45^\circ$ with the vertical.
Separation between spheres: $r = 2l\sin 45^\circ = 2(1)\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \sqrt{2}\text{ m}$.
For equilibrium: $\tan 45^\circ = \frac{F_e}{mg} \implies F_e = mg = 0.01 \times 10 = 0.1\text{ N}$.
Coulomb's law:
$$F_e = \frac{k q^2}{r^2} \implies 0.1 = \frac{(9 \times 10^9) q^2}{(\sqrt{2})^2} = \frac{9 \times 10^9 q^2}{2}$$
$$q^2 = \frac{0.2}{9 \times 10^9} = \frac{2}{9} \times 10^{-10}\text{ C}^2$$
$$q = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \times 10^{-5} \approx \frac{1.414}{3} \times 10^{-5} \approx 0.471 \times 10^{-5}\text{ C} = 4.71\,\mu\text{C} \approx 4.7\,\mu\text{C}$$
